Author: sim6572
Content:
Hello all,
I am an RTL designer with some knowledge on RTL GDSII flow. I am createding a chip with GP180 using LibreLane  flow. Chip seems ready for manufacturing because LibreLane flow ended without errors. However, an ASIC created using this RTL is already in production, but it was created by an external company using my RTL with proprietary PDK and commercial EDA tools. I successfully run my proven in use test cases  on the netlist with SDF coming from my open source flow, so I double-checked the outcome of the open source flow is correct. What concerned me s lot Is the speed degradation. Commercial ASIC is running at 75 MHz, my open source version is instead only 10 MHz capable at High temperature. So 7.5x degradation. I could expect something less performant  but not likes this. I have seen part of the gap is due to primitives, open-source libraries is offering less primitives and the ones equivalent are up to 2x slower, but where is coming from the other part of the gap? Can be explained by less optimized tools? Do you have any similar experience where you can compare the same device realized with proprietary ASIC flow and open source flow? Thanks for any hint.

Author: mole99
Content:
Hi @Simo6572,

Was your previous chip created using the same GF180MCU process and a proprietary PDK, or did you use a different process?

Note that the foundry-provided standard cell library in the open-source PDK uses the high-voltage transistors, which are slow. Tholin made a community-created standard cell library using the low-voltage transistors, which is much faster running at 3.3V. However, it hasn't been tested yet (the wafers are coming out of the fab this week).

Author: namibj
Content:
You'll have to use the Avalon Semiconductors 3v3 SCL to have a good chance; there's an SRAM compiler giving much better density than the foundry open PDK macros offer by @Chips4Makers aka Staf Verhaegen .

Note that the Avalon 3v3 SCL isn't currently too production-ready but that's mostly because there may be bugs left that haven't yet been caught through extracted SPICE behavioral sanity checking.
For purposes of determining if you can do an RTL on a wafer.space slot at least near a target speed, it should suffice.

Author: mole99
Content: Note that you can also use Tim Edwards' SRAM macros, which are shrinked versions of the foundry ones.

Author: mole99
Content: The project template allows you to choose the 3.3V SCL and SRAMs: https://github.com/wafer-space/gf180mcu-project-template#select-different-ip-libraries

Author: namibj
Content:
I'm not saying the shrunk foundry SRAM are wrong 😉

But Staf's periphery is far better at least at these sizes.
And should be much more amenable to learning how to be 10bit wide.
